term.def: The per-request bag hydrated once in middleware — who is asking, their active organization, their effective permissions, and the gated database handle. Every gated method takes it as its first parameter and passes it down; it is never recomputed per layer. Written `ac` in code.
The append-only journal of a location's decisions.
One universal invariant per line, most abstract first. No mechanism, no method names.
What a worker can do: a node of the capability tree of the [[ontology]].
A worker that asks the open API to charge credits. When a pipeline checks credits in the middle of a run it also charges, so parallel runs cannot overspend.
A worker, started every N minutes, that asks the open API which crons are due in the next N minutes and starts those pipelines.
A prebuilt slot wrapper from `@libs/web-layouts` — currently only `AuthPage`. Other pages assemble [[layout primitive|primitives]] via app-level section layouts (`PageFrame`, `SettingsLayout`).
The docs of a reusable domain about how to use it.
The docs of a reusable domain about how to change it.
Mechanically converted from markdown: axioms and purpose still to write, and nothing reviewed.
A worker that asks the open API for the credits, at the start of a run and, in a complex pipeline, again during it.
Only the open API knows the credits of a user or an organization: the orchestrator asks it.
A canonical document: axiom, purpose, reference.

The per-request database handle the access-control library hands out — the only thing in the system holding the connection. Its reads and writes require a [[scope]]; it never throws, returning no rows or null when access control admits nothing. Distinct from the unmet-requirements **gate**, which answers obligations and never touches data.
The terms of a location, cross-referenced with `[[term]]`.
The app supplying configs, slice infra (db), leaf adapters and assets to a [[slice]] at mount. Slices declare needs; they never import the concrete.
What is asked: a user intent at runtime, or a scheduled intent.
The open API accepts only the orchestrator's IPs; the main API accepts only clients'.

term.def: A component from `@libs/web-layouts` emitting one `layout="…"` region. Structural behaviour only — scroll, overflow, collapse, sticky, width — never visuals. Shell primitives are app-level only.
An abstract interface a [[slice]] declares for a swappable capability (toast, i18n); the app injects the concrete implementation at mount.
A low-level reusable engine in `shared/libs/<name>/`. Zero product knowledge, imports node modules only.
A fact-only event a [[slice]] emits about itself. The app decides what to do with it.
A folder of the repo that owns its docs: the root, main, a library, a slice, an app.
The entry point of a location's docs: its entries, with a summary and when to read each. Navigation only.
A file or folder that follows the rules of the mapper. The registry labels each one.
Map → Axioms → Purpose → Reference: the documentation standard.
The single touch point where the app instantiates a [[slice]], wires its hooks and injects its needs (`apps/main/shared/api/src/mounts.ts`).
The versioned trees of capabilities and tools. A worker is labelled for one version and can be relabelled when the ontology improves.
A second API instance, separate from the main API, that shares only the database connection string with it. Only the orchestrator reaches it.
A folder with its own `package.json`, imported by name rather than by path. Every [[library]], [[seed slice]], [[product slice]], config set and app is one.
Everything inside the shell content area — `page-header` plus `page-body` (`left-sidebar`, `main`, `right-sidebar`).

A leaf of the access-control config: one entity, the actions it covers, an optional column allowlist, and the rules that narrow it. Granted only by holding a role that carries it; permissions never nest.
Orchestrates [[worker|workers]] and other pipelines.
How a worker authenticates to the open API, since the user's JWT is not available to it.

term.def: Product-specific [[slice]] in `apps/main/slices/product/<s>/` — full-stack ([[slice app|slice apps]] + own `shared/`), same anatomy as a [[seed slice]], open import boundaries.
What a [[slice]] exports through its barrels (`api/index.ts`, `models/index.ts`, `web/index.ts`). Anything not in a barrel is internal and unreachable.
One paragraph: why the decisions exist. It does not restate the axioms.
One way to reach a goal with a [[pipeline]]. There can be several recipes per goal, and a benchmark picks the canonical one.
The concrete rules and mechanics, with diagrams over prose.
Which services the open API exposes.

issues: the path apps/main/shared/api/open-api does not exist

term.def: The global list of locations, each pointing at its map. It holds no content.
A library or a seed slice: its docs split into consumer and contributor.
The role hierarchy of one org type — an independent tree per type, plus the account baseline that applies with no org in context. A role resolves to every [[permission]] at or beneath it.
One execution of a pipeline. The orchestrator starts a run from a user request or from a scheduled trigger.

What the access-control engine returns for a read, update or delete: the compiled row filter for one entity and one action, plus the column allowlist. Branded by entity and action, and mintable only by the engine — the [[gated db]] refuses to run without the matching one, so an ungated query cannot compile.
A [[page]] whose `left-sidebar` navigates its [[sub-page|sub-pages]] — Settings, for example.
A self-contained, product-agnostic [[slice]] in `apps/main/slices/seed/<s>/`, reusable across projects. Ships with the seed.
The outermost viewport frame: `shell-side-nav`, `shell-top-nav` or `shell-none`. It decides what chrome surrounds the [[page]]. The app picks one per route.

One runtime facet of a [[slice]] — `api/`, `web/`, or `mobile/` inside a seed or product slice. Not independently deployable; compiles into the real `apps/main/shared/<app>/` it's mounted into. Named to echo `apps/` without colliding with it.
A [[seed slice|seed]] or [[product slice|product]] slice. The unit that owns entities, models and business logic.
The orchestrator holds no data and reads no database; it asks the open API for what it needs.
Real-time output of a run to the requester, over SSE, one stream per chat.
A page that fills `main` inside a [[section]], rather than the whole [[page]] region.
Services, repositories and models: the code both APIs share. Deployed, each API carries its own copy.
One of the levels code lives at: `configs`, `libs`, `slices`, `apps`. The tier fixes what something may import, and the import scope names it — `@modules/…`, `@libs/…`.
The routes and middleware of an API: the code written for it. The open API's transit imports the main API's services.
What starts a [[run]]: a user or a cron. An agent never starts anything: it acts inside a pipeline, on behalf of the user's request.
A task that runs and dies: an intent plus a tool with a closed contract. The output is the same per intent; the input and the config vary.
